heroText: Georgetown is Guyana's low-rise coastal capital, built around canals, wooden colonial architecture and a busy market-and-seawall rhythm. Start at St George's Cathedral, walk the Stabroek Market area in daylight, then use the Seawall or Promenade Gardens for a slower break. Cheddi Jagan airport handles international arrivals well outside the city, while Ogle is useful for domestic flights.

areas.name: Kingston
areas.text: Kingston is practical for business, embassies, waterfront access and established hotels north of the central market area.

areas.name: Stabroek
areas.text: Stabroek is central for markets, ferries and downtown errands, but it is busiest by day and needs more caution.

areas.name: Bourda
areas.text: Bourda is useful for local food, shopping and cricket-ground access, with a more everyday city feel.

areas.name: Queenstown
areas.text: Queenstown is a quieter residential base near central Georgetown, suitable for guesthouses and short taxi rides.

areas.name: Kitty
areas.text: Kitty sits toward the seawall and airport road, useful for local restaurants, guesthouses and easier coastal movement.

airports.name: Cheddi Jagan International Airport (GEO)
airports.search: Cheddi Jagan International Airport, Georgetown, Guyana
airports.text: Cheddi Jagan airport is south of Georgetown near Timehri; arrange transfers ahead because the road trip is substantial.

airports.name: Eugene F. Correia International Airport (OGL)
airports.search: Eugene F. Correia International Airport, Ogle, Guyana
airports.text: Ogle airport is closer to the city and is important for domestic flights, interior lodges and some regional services.

airportTransfer.value: 50-75 min by pre-arranged transfer from Timehri to central Georgetown

stayOverview: Use Kingston or Queenstown for the simplest Georgetown stay, especially for business, embassies or guesthouses. Stabroek is central but hectic, Bourda is practical for food and cricket, and Kitty helps with seawall access and coastal movement.
hotelIntro: Georgetown hotel choice is about transfers and comfort rather than walking everywhere: Kingston is the safest default, Queenstown is quieter, Stabroek is central by day, Bourda feels local, and Kitty works for seawall-side plans.
rentalCars: Most visitors should use taxis or arranged transfers in Georgetown; rent only for planned coastal or interior logistics.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Kingston or Queenstown for a first stay because they balance hotel comfort, taxis and access to central Georgetown.

travelTips.title: Airport transfers
travelTips.text: Pre-book Cheddi Jagan transfers, especially for late arrivals, because the airport is well outside the city.

travelTips.title: Safety
travelTips.text: Visit markets and downtown streets in daylight, use taxis at night and keep phones and valuables discreet.

travelTips.title: Interior trips
travelTips.text: Kaieteur Falls and rainforest lodges usually require flights or specialist operators, not casual same-day road planning.

highlights.title: St George's Cathedral
highlights.text: St George's Cathedral anchors the historic and ceremonial side of Georgetown, making it a practical stop for architecture, local memory and orientation.

highlights.title: Stabroek Market
highlights.text: Stabroek Market is the city's busy commercial heart, best visited in daylight for food, movement and local color.

highlights.title: Promenade Gardens
highlights.text: Promenade Gardens adds outdoor time to a Georgetown stay, with open space, views or waterfront breathing room between denser city sights.

highlights.title: National Museum of Guyana
highlights.text: National Museum of Guyana is a key Georgetown culture stop, useful for understanding local history, collections and rainy-day planning near the main sightseeing route.

highlights.title: Georgetown Seawall
highlights.text: Georgetown Seawall is a named Georgetown landmark that helps structure a real visit, adding orientation, local context and a clear route anchor.

highlights.title: Botanical Gardens
highlights.text: Botanical Gardens adds outdoor time to a Georgetown stay, with open space, views or waterfront breathing room between denser city sights.

nearbyIdeas.name: Kaieteur Falls
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Kaieteur Falls is Guyana's signature natural wonder, normally reached by scenic flight rather than road.

nearbyIdeas.name: Essequibo River
nearbyIdeas.label: River
nearbyIdeas.text: The Essequibo River offers islands, forts and lodge stays, best planned with a tour operator or driver.

nearbyIdeas.name: Parika
nearbyIdeas.label: River
nearbyIdeas.text: Parika is a river-port day trip west of Georgetown, useful for seeing ferry movement and market life.

history.text: In 1748, Governor Laurens Storm van 's Gravesande built a guard post at the mouth of the Demerara River.
The town was established in 1782 during a brief occupation by the French of the Dutch colony of Demerara.
The original name of Longchamps was changed to Stabroek in 1784, after Nicholaas Geelvinck (1732 — 1787), Lord of Stabroek, the then President of the Dutch West India Company.
The city's name changed again in 1812 when, under British rule, it became Georgetown, in honour of King George III.
Georgetown gained official city status on 24 August 1842 during the reign of Queen Victoria.
In 1945, a large fire (The Great Fire) broke out in the city, causing widespread damage.

history.text: American traders started to build a wharf which became known as American Stelling, and little towns started to appear around the main settlement.
